title: Preoperative Celecoxib and Acetaminophen Versus Acetaminophen Alone for Pain Control After Pediatric Adenotonsillectomy
official: An Open-Label, Randomized Study of Preoperative Celecoxib After Pediatric Adenotonsillectomy
summary: This is an open-label randomized study of approximately 500 pediatric patients (2-18 years of age, weighing more than 10 kg) undergoing adenotonsillectomy. Participants are assigned to a preoperative multimodal analgesic regimen (oral celecoxib the evening before and the morning of surgery, plus intra-operative dexamethasone and acetaminophen) or to standard of care (no pre-operative medication; intra-operative dexamethasone and acetaminophen). The primary aim is to compare postoperative pain control, measured by rescue analgesic consumption, over the first 72 hours after surgery. Secondary aims assess safety (postoperative bleeding and adverse medication events) and feasibility (healthcare utilization and caregiver satisfaction).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Pediatric patients 2-18 years of age
* Weighing greater than 10 kg
* Undergoing adenotonsillectomy
* English- or Spanish-speaking patients

Exclusion Criteria:

* Any adjunct procedure other than bilateral myringotomy tubes (BMT) or direct laryngoscopy and bronchoscopy (DLB) without bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL)
* Bleeding disorders
* Allergy to NSAIDs
* Allergy to acetaminophen (Tylenol)
* Pregnancy
